speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
title: Teach Truth with Love
session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

points.text: Elder Clark G. Gilbert spoke about “Teach Truth with Love”.

quotes.text: It takes courage to stand for truth. It takes even more courage to stand for truth with love. President Dallin H. Oaks has repeatedly emphasized this message. Last general conference he explained the challenge: “When we seek to keep all the commandments in our personal lives, we are sometimes accused of having no love for those who don’t. When we show personal love and support loving causes, we are sometimes misunderstood as implying support for results that contradict our … religious duties.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Consider Dostoevsky’s literary description of Christ and the Grand Inquisitor. After repeatedly being denounced, the Savior simply kissed His accuser with no further response. In a lesser way, I recently felt this when a group of national academic leaders aggressively criticized the role of faith in higher education. Recognizing the escalating tension of the moment, I chose at least for that setting to table the discussion despite my strong disagreement with what was being said.
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: I failed to see this with a friend who had at one time been spiritually faithful but was now attacking the Church. My frustration came not just because of his bitterness but because I knew he knew better. Unfortunately, rather than recognize the tension of the moment or that he might be hurting for reasons I could not see, I shot back an angry retort. I may have won the debate in the moment, but I lost the Spirit and I failed to help my struggling friend. That day I stood for truth, but I did it without love and without charity.
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: The third principle is to be a light. President Nelson taught: “Let your skeptical friends see how much you love the Lord and His gospel. Surprise their doubting hearts with your believing heart!” The best way to help someone else keep their covenants is to keep your covenants. As Sister Tamara Runia reminded us, “Stay at the tree, … continue to beckon to those you love … that eating the fruit is a happy thing!”
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Now, the fourth principle is to hold to truth even in our outreach. In April, President Oaks stated that showing love for others “does not mean surrendering our values. The covenants we have made inevitably position us as devoted participants in the eternal contest between truth and error.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Some have argued that loving our neighbor (the second commandment) somehow supersedes or takes priority over loving God (the first commandment). But President D. Todd Christofferson pointed out: “Putting the first commandment first does not diminish or limit our ability to keep the second commandment. To the contrary, it amplifies and strengthens it. … Our love of God elevates our ability to love others more fully and perfectly because we in essence partner with God in the care of His children.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: When we try to love others by minimizing God’s laws, we separate ourselves from the one person who loves them the very most. The Savior showed love for the woman taken in adultery. But He also charged her to “go, and sin no more.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together. I believe teaching truth with love will be the hallmark of Christ’s disciples in the last days. For some this will require greater conviction. For others it will demand greater charity. I know the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
quotes.speaker: Elder Clark G. Gilbert
quotes.session: Sunday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference
